chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, from Hammad ibn 'Isa, from Shu'ayb, from Abi Basir, from Abi 'Abd Allah عليه السلام, who said:

The takbirs in al-Fitr and al-Adha are twelve takbirs: you say one takbir in the first rak'ah, then recite, then after the recitation you say five takbirs, and with the seventh you perform ruku'. Then you rise in the second rak'ah and recite, then say four takbirs, and with the fifth you perform ruku'.

key_terms.التَّكْبِيرُ: The saying of 'Allahu Akbar' within the prayer sequence.
key_terms.الْأَضْحَى: The 'Eid of sacrifice, referring to 'Eid al-Adha.
key_terms.الْفِطْرِ: The 'Eid of breaking the fast, referring to 'Eid al-Fitr.
key_terms.الْقِرَاءَةِ: The recitation in the prayer before the additional takbirs.
key_terms.تَرْكَعُ: You perform ruku' with that takbir.
key_terms.تَكْبِيرَةً: A single utterance of takbir counted within the prayer.

ai.seo_question: How are the takbirs performed in Salat al-'Eidayn according to Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the manner of the takbirs in the salat of the two 'Eids, al-Fitr and al-Adha. It specifies the number and placement of the takbirs in each rak'ah, making it a practical legal text in the rulings of worship.
